chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about salat (prayer) in the houses of the Magians while they are sprinkled with water, and he said: “There is no harm in it.”

Then he said: “And I saw him on the road to Makkah at times sprinkling the place of his forehead, then performing sajdah (prostration) upon it while it was damp as it was; and perhaps at times he did not sprinkle the place which he considered to be clean.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship being discussed
key_terms.بُيُوتِ: houses or dwellings, referring to the location of prayer
key_terms.بِالْمَاءِ: with water, the means used for sprinkling
key_terms.تُرَشُّ: is sprinkled, referring to sprinkling water on the place
key_terms.جَبْهَتِهِ: his forehead, the part placed on the ground in sajdah (prostration)
key_terms.نَظِيفٌ: clean, describing the state of the place

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in the houses of the Magians if the place is sprinkled with water?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that there is no harm in performing salat (prayer) in the houses of the Magians when the place is sprinkled with water. It also describes a practical example related to preparing the place of sajdah (prostration), showing attention to cleanliness while indicating that sprinkling was not necessary when the place was regarded as clean.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.730 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about praying in the houses of the Magians (Zoroastrians) if they are sprinkled with water, and He said:
"There is no harm in it."

He then mentioned that he sometimes saw someone on the road to Makkah sprinkling water on the spot where they placed their forehead before prostrating, while at other times, they did not sprinkle water if they deemed the place to be clean.
